learningGoals: Count confidently and recognize numbers from 21 to 99. 🚂
Understand the basic concept of tens and ones using everyday objects. 🧱
Identify and complete simple number patterns and sequences. 🧩
Develop a joyful and fearless attitude towards bigger numbers! 🌟
teachingTips: Use physical items like pebbles, kidney beans, or beads to make counting abstract numbers feel real and touchable. 🧮
Point out numbers between 21 and 99 in daily life, such as house numbers, page numbers in a book, or bus numbers. 🚌
Focus on the joy of playing with numbers rather than just getting the right answer to build their confidence! 💖
Practice counting backwards from 50 or playing 'what number comes next' during car rides or walks. 🚶‍♂️

funActivities.title: Bundle of Tens 🥢
funActivities.description: Give your child a handful of toothpicks, crayons, or matchsticks. Help them tie them into bundles of 10 using rubber bands. Ask them to show you numbers like 34 by picking 3 bundles and 4 loose sticks! 🎀

funActivities.title: Number Hopscotch 🏃‍♀️
funActivities.description: Draw a hopscotch grid with chalk, but instead of 1 to 10, write numbers like 21, 22, 23, up to 30. Ask your child to shout the numbers loud and clear as they jump! 🖍️

funActivities.title: The Missing Number Detective 🕵️‍♂️
funActivities.description: Write a sequence of numbers from 41 to 50 on small pieces of paper and line them up. While your child closes their eyes, take one away. Ask them to open their eyes and guess the missing number! 🔍
